referenceDayRule: The anchor every seeded day is written against, and the app rolls the whole seed onto the day Prep reads (`seedDay` in `supplier-payments.ts`). So `due`, `delivered`, `paid`, `since`, `asOf`, the three windows and `inLineSince` keep their distance from this day, and Money and Prep name one day on every date the app is opened.
amounts: integers in minor units, as Cedar's money model stores them

rules.amounts: Every figure is an integer in minor units under `money`, `prepDay` and `record`. A currency token appears in this file nowhere, so the price grep reads it clean.
rules.chatPrices: `chatCorpus` carries figures nowhere: the seeded messages state quantities, days and names. An amount enters the book when the shop confirms a row with its own act.
rules.phones: Customer i takes +51 9{70+i} {400+3i} {100+7i}; supplier s takes +51 9{50+s} {600+3s} {300+7s}. Each is unique, reproducible from its own row, and shaped like a Peruvian mobile.
rules.derived: Every generated credit, sale, receipt and reason line is a pure function of its row's own index, so the same morning returns on every reload.
rules.coordinates: Locations are block words. The file holds coordinates nowhere, so the map stays off Prep.

customerRules.names: The shop's own WhatsApp contact names, which is what the read returns — a bodeguera's phone holds people, so half-labels stand: `Rosa menú`, `Elmer taxi`, `Julia 2do piso`.
customerRules.settles: Nine fiado, nine cash. Six of the nine fiado customers owe today.
customerRules.bands: A neighbour buys inside 1500–8000 minor units; a business inside 12000–40000.

supplierRules.bread: Bread drops every morning at its own per-drop band and settles on Saturdays, which is the figure the payables card carries.
supplierRules.payLater: The four on a week's terms are the pay-later candidates: `pollo`, `lacteos`, `abarrotes`, `limpieza`. Aurora is the biggest, so its card carries the 30-day settlement.
supplierRules.purchases: `purchases` is the orders the shop's chat with that supplier shows over the window, in the supplier's own rhythm: bread drops daily and leads with 22, chicken comes four mornings a week, the mayorista and the distributor twice, the gas man on call and reads 3. It is the figure the referral row prints as `Bought 22 times`, so the count ranks the suppliers the way the week does.
supplierRules.referrals: The referral unit is suppliers: each one that joins is one more the shop can pay later, and that sentence ships once a lender is signed.

chatCorpus.priceRule: A seeded message states quantities, days and names. Figures stay out, so the read draws reasons in words and asserts a total nowhere.
chatCorpus.imageRule: An image message is stored as its caption alone while media custody stays unbuilt: a Yape or Plin voucher reads as `[image]` plus what was written beside it.
chatCorpus.register: Lima, lowercase, few accents: `casera`, `porfa`, `al cuaderno`, `ya te yapeé`.

whoOwesYou.heading: likely, until the shop confirms each row
whoOwesYou.recencyRule: `lastOrderDaysAgo` is the READ's own answer over the projected chats (`history/read.ts`), and `app/tools/test-bodega-history.mjs` holds the two equal row by row — so this figure is changed there, never here. It counts the newest order in the CHAT CORPUS, which is a different book from `prepDay`: Maribel reads `last order yesterday` while Prep times her order this morning, and reconciling the two belongs to the read.
whoOwesYou.rule: Rank on the chat's own evidence: fiado asked for, orders with a payment message missing after them, how recent, how often. Each row prints its reason in words, states an amount only where a message states one, and the confirmation is what the fiado book records.

prepDay.ordersRule: `received`, `lines` and `state` are what `cast-cedar.ts` builds for these twelve accounts, read back off the fold and pinned here, so a customer sheet and the Prep row name one order with one line count. A quantity lives here nowhere: `qtyFor` sizes every line and `wholeUnits` keeps a unit whole.
prepDay.order: `To review` first, then the groups, orders by arrival.
prepDay.counts: Prep counts read `sales`, the record is a `Sale`, and the export runs by transaction and by customer.

bank.sunatNote: The balance stays far under the 7 UIT monthly line, which is why the shop's own export is its record.

incoming30d.matchRule: A matched credit carries `Receipt.status: 'matched'`; counter takings land in the day's figure, and a credit colliding on an amount lands in `review`.

fiadoBook.reminderRule: A fiado reminder states the sale, the amount and the date, and it carries a fee nowhere.
fiadoBook.confirmation: Each row here stands because the shop confirmed it on the read screen; the corpus itself states amounts nowhere.

rows.state: due the day before the reference day, so it reads one day late on every clock

settled.note: paid on the day, 2 days early

payables.payLater: Pay-later is one record per purchase, settled at 30 days. The file holds a limit, a rate and a date nowhere, and `advanceLimitOf` stays unread.

indicators.newestReason: Paid on the day · Distribuidora Aurora, 2 days early · confirmed by your bank

record.reasonRule: A reason states the fact alone; the day it carries is the day the app is read on, so `money-overview.tsx` writes `19 Sep · A sale recorded today` off the same clock Prep reads.
record.levelRule: `Starting` while an indicator sits under its floor; `Steady` at 80 / 60 / 70 per cent or better; `Punctual` with every supplier payment in the 90 days paid on or before the day. The one late payable holds this shop at `Steady`.
record.reads: The shop's own behaviour alone. Its customers' punctuality prints as its own ledger, and a third party in its chats stays unprofiled.

queue.placeRule: The SAMPLE world's own waitlist place, its referral code and the two constants screen 9 states. The rig reads all four from `GET /api/bodega/waitlist`; these stand where no connection service answers, and the screen prints `Sample waitlist` beside them (ONBOARDING-SPEC.md §0).
